detail:
Cleveland Clinic describes treatment that focuses on the underlying cause and on easing painful symptoms. About half of small fiber neuropathy cases happen for no known reason; when a cause is identified, such as diabetes, a vitamin deficiency, an infection, or a toxin exposure, treating that condition is part of slowing the neuropathy.

For pain, Cleveland Clinic lists medicines clinicians may prescribe, including anti-seizure medications such as gabapentin, pregabalin, or topiramate, certain antidepressants such as amitriptyline or nortriptyline, and topical anesthetics such as lidocaine or capsaicin. It also describes pain management programs that combine counseling and therapy, exercise, and hands-on treatment such as massage or physical therapy.

Talk to your doctor before starting or changing any medication.

Tabs is not endorsing or verifying this material.
summary: Cleveland Clinic describes two-track care for small fiber neuropathy: treat the underlying condition when one is found, and manage neuropathic pain with medicines such as certain anti-seizure drugs, antidepressants, or topical treatments chosen by a clinician.
takeaways: finding and treating a cause can slow progression
about half of cases have no cause found
pain medicines for sfn are prescription decisions
pain programs can add therapy, exercise, and counseling
title: Managing small fiber neuropathy: treat the cause, ease the pain
